name: Copper
tagline: Run a basic sales pipeline closely tied to Google Workspace data

tiers.name: Basic
tiers.limits: 2,500 contacts; task automation, pipelines, projects and contact enrichment

tiers.name: Professional
tiers.limits: 15,000 contacts; workflow automation, bulk email, reporting and integrations

tiers.name: Business
tiers.limits: Unlimited contacts; email series, custom reports, multi-currency and premium support

pricing.freeTierCaps: no free tier (free trial; no credit card required)
pricing.hiddenCosts: Prices exclude applicable taxes and fees. Personal onboarding and premium support are limited to eligible Professional/Business annual accounts.

verdictSummary: The core loop is buildable, but a dependable replacement becomes a real weekend or multi-day project. For Copper, run a basic sales pipeline closely tied to Google Workspace data. The hard boundary is gmail and calendar integration, automatic activity capture, reporting, and support, plus integrations, data quality, and workflow lock-in.
coreLoopDIY: Manage contacts and companies tied to Google Workspace data, move opportunities through a basic pipeline, log interactions, and surface the next action.
whatYouLose: Gmail and Calendar integration, automatic activity capture, reporting, and support
moatNotes: integrations, data quality, and workflow lock-in
ongoingBurden: deduplication, permissions, imports, sync, enrichment, email capture, automations, backups, and audit history
whyPeopleStillPay: People still pay for Copper because CRM value compounds as the system becomes the shared memory of every customer interaction and embeds itself in the rest of the stack. The recurring cost buys deduplication, permissions, imports, sync, enrichment, email capture, automations, backups, and audit history, not just the visible interface.

priorArt.name: Twenty
priorArt.desc: Active open-source modern CRM with extensible data models.

alternatives.name: HubSpot Free CRM
alternatives.desc: A real two-seat CRM for free; 1,000 contacts is where the upsell starts counting.

facts.install: Hosted signup; optionally connect/import email, calendar, and contacts
facts.dataFormat: Structured CRM customer records stored and processed on HubSpot's cloud servers, with regional hosting options and exports
facts.gapVsPaid: HubSpot’s Gmail integration is useful but less deeply embedded in Google Workspace and less automatic about associating mail, files, and calendar context than Copper.

alternatives.name: Twenty
alternatives.desc: A modern pipeline CRM with custom objects, views and mailbox sync; the subscription becomes a Compose file.

facts.install: Hosted cloud signup or official one-line/Docker Compose self-host install
facts.dataFormat: CRM records and configuration in PostgreSQL; files in local storage or S3-compatible object storage on the selected host
facts.gapVsPaid: Twenty can synchronize mailboxes and calendars but remains a separate CRM rather than Copper’s Google-Workspace-native layer.
facts.setupBlocker: Free use requires Docker, at least 2 GB RAM, PostgreSQL-backed containers, secrets, and domain/TLS configuration

alternatives.name: Odoo CRM One App Free
alternatives.desc: A hosted pipeline with Google Calendar sync; not quite living inside Workspace.

facts.install: Hosted Odoo Online signup with CRM selected as the single free app
facts.dataFormat: Structured Odoo records in an Odoo-hosted customer database; records can be exported from list views
facts.gapVsPaid: Odoo can connect Google Calendar, but it does not match Copper’s tight Gmail, Drive, and Workspace context.

alternatives.name: Zoho CRM Free
alternatives.desc: A three-user pipeline with Gmail and Calendar connections; the interface remains unmistakably Zoho.

facts.dataFormat: Structured CRM service data stored on Zoho's cloud servers; Zoho states users can access, export, and delete service data
facts.gapVsPaid: Zoho’s Google integrations work beside a standalone CRM and feel less seamless than Copper’s native Workspace-centered workflow.

notes: Editorial comparison targets the Basic plan and a personal or very small-team CRM DIY substitute. Recheck price before merge.
prompt:
Build a personal replacement for Copper in an empty repository.
Use Next.js 15, TypeScript, PostgreSQL, Drizzle ORM, and Docker Compose; do not offer alternative stacks.
The core loop is: manage contacts and companies tied to Google Workspace data, move opportunities through a basic pipeline, log interactions, and surface the next action.
Make the first run work locally with one documented command.
Store all user data locally by default and make export straightforward.
Put secrets in .env, ship .env.example, and never commit credentials.
Create contacts, companies, opportunities, notes, tasks, and configurable pipeline stages.
Add fast global search, duplicate detection, merge, CSV import, and CSV export.
Provide a chronological interaction timeline with manual email and meeting logging.
Implement saved views, filters, owner assignment, and a next-action dashboard.
Add role-based access, an immutable activity log, backups, and a recovery command.
Seed a realistic demo workspace and document field mapping for imports.
Include clear empty, loading, success, and recoverable error states.
Add input validation, safe filenames, and graceful handling of unavailable APIs.
Write focused tests for the core transformation and one end-to-end happy path.
Create a README with setup, architecture, permissions, data location, and backup steps.
Do not add accounts, billing, telemetry, analytics, or a hosted control plane.
Deliberately leave out automatic mailbox ingestion.
Deliberately leave out commercial enrichment databases.
Deliberately leave out enterprise forecasting, integrations, and compliance.
Finish by running the tests and listing the exact commands used.
